newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch Nutricia bans modified soya from baby milk.
newsitem.headline: Dutch Nutricia bans modified soya from baby milk.

text.p: Dutch food group Nutricia said on Thursday that for time being its infant milk formulas would not be made from genetically-altered soybeans.

"We feel there is still a lot of discussion going on in the German speaking markets on this and while this is happening we should not bring products containing these beans to the market," spokesman Klaas de Jong told Reuters.

But he added the company only used very small quantities of soya proteins in some special baby milk formulas and that consumer feeling in Germany and Austria was such to make it unrealistic to produce two separate types for European markets.
De Jong stressed the company believed the tests carried out by U.S. and European authorities on the new beans were adequate but it had taken the decision because "the client was king".
He said it was not a problem for Nutricia to guarantee the non-usage of genetically-altered beans because it had stocks of normal beans sufficient to last 16 months.
He added that he thought the problem could be eventually solved by companies guaranteeing to supply normal beans.
"If it is proved that this is what the market wants, then it will happen," he said.
